from.place: Second proof paragraph: conjugation by the same reconstruction, projection-formula, and direct-image/limit isomorphisms; coefficient normalization for intermediate complete inputs.

title: Coefficient normalization of the raw ordered completed exchange
statement:
Fix a cartesian square of schemes $\square=(f:X\to Y,f':X'\to Y',g:Y'\to Y,g':X'\to X)$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], and the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $A$ is commutative Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated, $A/I$ is additive torsion, and every $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite and perfect over $A$. Put $A_T=\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}_T$ on the small pro-etale site of each corner $T$, with the canonical map $\underline A_T\to A_T$. Let $\operatorname{Res}_T$ be derived restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Use the canonical coefficient isomorphisms $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] and the ringed operations over $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the strict reduction tower functor $\mathcal R^a_T$ of the datum, and completed pullback $F^a_u$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Let $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$, with $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ on its derived category and strict constant-coefficient reduction functor $\mathcal R_T$ as in [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison]. For an edge $u:U\to V$, write $G_u=u^{-1}$ termwise, $R_u^{\mathcal T}$ for derived termwise direct image, $R_u^0=Ru_*$ on constant-coefficient complexes, $C_T=\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_T$, and $F_u^0=C_UG_u$ on the full derived-complete categories [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. All sites and diagram sites are small in the convention of [def-weil-size-convention].

Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$ be any derived $I$-complete object, meaning that the canonical quotient completion map $K\to\mathcal L^a_X\mathcal R^a_XK$ is invertible [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], and put $\bar K=\operatorname{Res}_XK$. No properness, constructibility, boundedness, or etale-origin hypothesis is imposed. Use derived strict-tower operations $\mathscr L_u,\mathscr R_u$ over $A_T$, computed on the diagram sites [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Define the raw ordered construction as follows, before choosing any finite etale-origin witnesses. Put $E=Lg'^*K$, $M=Lg^*Rf_*K$, $N=Rf'_*E$, and let $e:M\to N$ be the ambient ringed adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Let
$$B^a=\mathscr L_g\mathscr R_f\mathcal R^a_XK,\qquad D^a=\mathscr R_{f'}\mathscr L_{g'}\mathcal R^a_XK.$$
Let $H^a:\mathcal R^a_{Y'}M\xrightarrow{\sim}B^a$ and $H'^a:\mathcal R^a_{Y'}N\xrightarrow{\sim}D^a$ be the diagram-site projection-formula maps (adjuncts of counit tensored with identity [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]), with the canonical derived pullback/tensor isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] on these ringed diagram sites, using the coefficient identifications $u^{-1}\underline{P_n}_V\cong\underline{P_n}_U$ and $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$ fixed above. Their inverses exist by perfection of the $P_n$. Set
$$v^a=H'^a\mathcal R^a_{Y'}(e)(H^a)^{-1},\qquad s^a=\mathcal L^a(H^a)r_S,\qquad c^a:Rf'_*F^a_{g'}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L^aD^a,$$
where $\mathcal L^a$ is derived strict inverse limit with completed coefficients [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality], $r_S:F^a_gRf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L^a\mathcal R^a_{Y'}M$ is the quotient reconstruction identification of completed pullback, and $c^a$ is the specified direct-image/limit comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Put $x^a_K=(c^a)^{-1}\mathcal L^a(v^a)s^a$.

The following comparisons and equations hold in the derived strict-tower categories and derived module categories, naturally for all morphisms of complete $K$.

(1) Restriction commutes canonically with derived direct image on ambient complexes:
$$\chi_u:\operatorname{Res}_VRu_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R_u^0\operatorname{Res}_U.$$
On complete objects it identifies the completed adjunctions, with their units and counits, under the equivalences of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]:
$$\phi_u:\operatorname{Res}_UF^a_u\xrightarrow{\sim}F_u^0\operatorname{Res}_V.$$
Here $F^a_u\dashv Ru_*$ is the adjunction induced by ordinary module pullback/direct image and the completion reflector; $\phi_u$ is the isomorphism respecting their hom-set bijections and completion units. In particular these comparisons identify the canonical composition and identity comparisons defined as adjunction conjugates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of direct-image composition and identity. The equivalences do not identify the ambient constant and completed module categories.

(2) There is an isomorphism of actual derived strict towers
$$\rho_K:\operatorname{Res}_X\mathcal R^a_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal R_X\bar K,$$
induced by derived tensor reassociation on the ringed diagram site and its single strict quotient diagram; it respects the quotient-tower unit. Put $B^0=G_gR_f^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_X\bar K$, $D^0=R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}G_{g'}\mathcal R_X\bar K$. There are canonical tower isomorphisms
$$\beta:\operatorname{Res}_{Y'}B^a\xrightarrow{\sim}B^0,\qquad \delta:\operatorname{Res}_{Y'}D^a\xrightarrow{\sim}D^0.$$
Let $H^0:\mathcal R_{Y'}(G_gR_f^0\bar K)\to B^0$ be exactly the diagram projection-formula comparison in [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison]. There is a canonical isomorphism $\rho_M:\operatorname{Res}_{Y'}\mathcal R^a_{Y'}M\to\mathcal R_{Y'}(G_gR_f^0\bar K)$, obtained from the finite-reduction scalar comparisons, $\chi_f$, and derived pullback/tensor reassociation on that diagram site. They satisfy
$$\beta\operatorname{Res}(H^a)=H^0\rho_M,\qquad \delta\operatorname{Res}(v^a)=E^{\mathcal T}_{\mathcal R_X\bar K}\beta,$$
where $E^{\mathcal T}$ is the strict constant-coefficient adjunction mate of [def-weil-pbc-strict-tower-operations]. In the witnessed proper situation of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization], these $\beta,\delta$ are its specified $b,d$ followed by the images of $\rho_K$. Its specified towers and witness-transported $v'_\bullet$ agree with $B^a,D^a,v^a$. Thus $x^a_K$ is exactly the ordered completed exchange of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] whenever the witnesses required there are provided, independently of their choice. Equality here is in the derived strict-tower category, not inferred from evaluations.

(3) Write $\lambda_Z:\operatorname{Res}\mathcal L^a Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L\operatorname{Res}Z$ for the canonical restriction/derived-limit comparison, computed on strict K-injective models. Let $s^0:F_g^0R_f^0\bar K\to\mathcal L B^0$ and $t^0:R_{f'}^0F_{g'}^0\bar K\to\mathcal L D^0$ be exactly $s,t$ of [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison]. Put
$$\iota_S=(F_g^0\chi_f)\phi_g:\operatorname{Res}(F^a_gRf_*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_g^0R_f^0\bar K,\qquad \iota_T=(R_{f'}^0\phi_{g'})\chi_{f'}:\operatorname{Res}(Rf'_*F^a_{g'}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{f'}^0F_{g'}^0\bar K.$$
Both reconstruction identifications and the direct-image comparison have the following fixed normalization:
$$\mathcal L(\rho_M)\lambda_{\mathcal R^a M}\operatorname{Res}(r_S)=r_S^0\iota_S,\qquad \mathcal L(\rho_{g',K})\lambda_{\mathscr L_{g'}\mathcal R^a K}\operatorname{Res}(r_{g',K})=r_{g',K}^0\phi_{g'},$$
where $r_{g',K}:F^a_{g'}K\to\mathcal L^a(\mathscr L_{g'}\mathcal R^a_XK)$ is the defining reconstruction, $r_{g',K}^0:F_{g'}^0\bar K\to\mathcal L G_{g'}\mathcal R_X\bar K$ is its constant-coefficient counterpart, and $\rho_{g',K}:\operatorname{Res}\mathscr L_{g'}\mathcal R^a_XK\to G_{g'}\mathcal R_X\bar K$ is the same diagram-site finite-reduction scalar comparison. Here $r_S^0$ is the source reconstruction in the definition of $s^0$. Consequently
$$\mathcal L(\beta)\lambda_{B^a}\operatorname{Res}(s^a)=s^0\iota_S,\qquad \mathcal L(\delta)\lambda_{D^a}\operatorname{Res}(c^a)=t^0\iota_T.$$
In particular the equation for the raw ordered exchange is
$$\iota_T\operatorname{Res}(x^a_K)= (t^0)^{-1}\mathcal L(E^{\mathcal T}_{\mathcal R_X\bar K})s^0\iota_S.$$
All displayed comparisons are the specified scalar, projection-formula, completion-unit and direct-image/limit comparisons. The equations are natural-transformation equations on the full derived-complete category, valid without witnesses also at complete inputs obtained by completed pullback or derived direct image. No identity-square or pasting law for exchange is asserted here.

source.place: Second paragraph, specified conjugating maps; agent-supplied strict coefficient comparison supplement. Ingredient sources only: proetale.tex Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), Tag 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), Tag 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram). None states this combined comparison.

proof.text: Write $r_T=\operatorname{Res}_T$, and distinguish the one-object indexing category from $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$. The coefficient maps commute with $\underline A\to A_T$: on constant sections both composites send $a$ to its image, and the finite projections determine the map to $A_U$. The profinite inverse-image lemma supplies both the coefficient isomorphisms and their composition/transition compatibility. Flatness of $A_T$ over $\underline A_T$ is supplied by the constant-completion equivalence. Apply the flat ringed diagram restriction theorem first with the one-object category and then with $J$. All sites are small; its scalar-square and flatness hypotheses have just been checked. In the first application it gives $a_u:r_ULu_a^*\simeq G_ur_V$ and $\chi_u:r_VRu_*\simeq R_u^0r_U$ on AMBIENT module complexes, with the stated adjunct compatibility. In the second it gives $p_u:r_U\mathscr L_u\simeq G_ur_V$ and $d_u:r_V\mathscr R_u\simeq R_u^{\mathcal T}r_U$. These use the identified underlying inverse image and direct image on a K-injective model. Explicitly the left adjoint of restriction is $A_T\otimes_{\underline A_T}-$, exact by flatness; the right-adjoint K-injective theorem applies for this reason, not merely because restriction itself is exact.

source.place: Second paragraph: ambient and diagram coefficient comparisons; Stacks 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), flat scalar case

proof.text:
For an ARBITRARY completed-coefficient tower $Z$, apply the ringed tower pushforward/limit comparison to the identity geometric morphism with structure map $\underline A_T\to A_T$. Its module direct image is restriction; restriction is exact, so its derived functor is $r_T$. This gives $\lambda_Z:r_T\mathcal L^aZ\simeq\mathcal Lr_TZ$, without a finite-reduction hypothesis. Check its normalization together with direct image as follows. Choose a K-injective tower $Z\to J_Z$; such resolutions exist since the small module diagram categories are Grothendieck. Restriction preserves its K-injectivity by Step 1. Also $\lim J_Z$ is K-injective: $\lim$ is right adjoint to the exact constant-diagram functor, so the right-adjoint theorem applies. For each edge the ordinary and diagram direct images preserve K-injectives, since their identified inverse images are exact. Thus $J_Z,rJ_Z,u_*J_Z,\lim J_Z$ compute the required derived composites. Denote their direct-image/limit comparisons by $\kappa_u^a,\kappa_u^0$. On these models the two routes below are the SAME equality of complexes, $r_Vu_*\lim J_Z=\lim u_*r_UJ_Z$:
$$\mathcal L(d_{u,Z})\lambda_{\mathscr R_uZ}r_V(\kappa_u^a(Z))=\kappa_u^0(r_UZ)R_u^0(\lambda_Z)\chi_{u,\mathcal L^aZ}.$$
The K-injective total-derived theorem identifies these models with the canonical derived functors. This proves compatibility of the specified comparisons, not uniqueness from their finite projections.

source.place: Second paragraph: direct-image/limit conjugations; Stacks 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), first proof on tower sites

proof.text: The diagram-site realization identifies strict towers with modules on one small ringed site, with ring $\Delta A_T$. For this $J$, object $1$ is terminal, so $\operatorname{colim}_J=\operatorname{ev}_1$ is exact. Its right adjoint $\Delta$ therefore preserves K-injectives by the right-adjoint theorem. An ambient K-injective representative $I_K$ consequently computes $\mathscr R_f\Delta K=\Delta Rf_*K$ by the same complex $\Delta f_*I_K$; the same argument applies to $f'$ and any ambient input $E$. A diagonal flat-term K-flat representative is K-flat on the diagram site: its tensor with an acyclic diagram is acyclic at every level, hence acyclic by levelwise cohomology. Existence of the ambient representative and the derived tensor comparison are supplied by the K-flat resolution and tensor-descent nodes. On these representatives the diagonal adjunction bijections are the componentwise ordinary ones. The characterization of the derived bijection on fraction representatives therefore identifies diagonal units and counits with the ambient ones. Pullback composition is termwise as well. By the mate's transpose formula the diagram exchange on $\Delta K$ is $\Delta e$. This comparison uses no properness or finite-origin witnesses.

source.place: Second paragraph: actual strict-diagram construction; expanded diagonal argument corresponding to normalization lemma Step 2

proof.text:
On the diagram site, the constant-completion equivalence applies to $\Delta\underline A_T\to\Delta A_T$: constant sheaves and limits are fiberwise under the diagram-site equivalence. Apply its finite-reduction comparison to $\Delta K$. The strict tensor construction gives
$$\rho_K:r_X\mathcal R_X^aK\simeq\mathcal R_X\bar K.$$
On a flat-term K-flat representative $P$, both sides are the SAME quotient diagram $(P/I^nP)_n$ with its quotient transitions; the map sends the class of $p$ to itself. Thus it respects the quotient unit as well. The derived tensor/pullback comparison and the coefficient identities identify $\mathcal R_U^aLu_a^*L$ with $\mathscr L_u\mathcal R_V^aL$. Combining this with $p_u$ and the preceding balancing map gives $\rho_{u,L}:r_U\mathscr L_u\mathcal R_V^aL\simeq G_u\mathcal R_Vr_VL$. These are strict-diagram comparisons, natural in $L$. Define
$$\beta=(G_gR_f^{\mathcal T}\rho_K)(G_gd_f)p_g,\qquad
\delta=(R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}G_{g'}\rho_K)(R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}p_{g'})d_{f'}.$$
Finally $\rho_M$ is the same reduction comparison for $M$, followed by $\mathcal R(a_g)$ and $\mathcal R(G_g\chi_f)$. These formulas give exactly the source, target and coefficient identifications specified in (2).

source.place: Second paragraph: strict finite-reduction and pullback/tensor identifications

proof.text:
Check the projection-formula equation by transposition, rather than by evaluations. On each coefficient diagram the projection map is the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes1)t_f$. The adjunct clause of flat diagram restriction identifies its restricted adjunct with the adjunct of its restricted transpose, and in particular identifies the restricted counit with the constant-coefficient counit. Under $\rho$, the tensor factor in that transpose is a quotient: on a K-flat representative the comparison is $p\otimes\bar a\mapsto p\otimes\bar a$, and the pullback/tensor comparison sends it to $(p\otimes1)\otimes\bar a$. Applying a morphism $h$ before or after either map sends it to $(h(p)\otimes1)\otimes\bar a$. Use this with the counit and the identified pullback. Hence the restricted transpose is exactly $(\varepsilon^0_{f,\bar K}\otimes1)t_f^0$. Bijectivity of the adjunct correspondence identifies the two projection maps. Apply $G_g$ and use the formulas for $\beta,\rho_M$ in Step 4 to obtain
$$\beta\,r(H^a)=H^0\rho_M.$$
This is an equality of derived diagram morphisms: the tensor comparisons come from natural maps on the resolving class, and tensor descent makes their equality an equality after localization. No general monoidal identification of the two ambient scalar categories is used.

source.place: Second paragraph: compatibility of the specified projection-formula conjugating map; Stacks 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map

proof.text:
Let $W$ be the completed-coefficient strict-diagram exchange at $\mathcal R_X^aK$, defined by its adjunction mate. Apply ringed exchange/tensor coherence on the completed ringed diagram sites with object $\Delta K$ and coefficient object $Q_{Y,\bullet}=(\underline{P_n}_Y)_n$. This theorem allows arbitrary ringed topoi and needs no properness. The coefficient isomorphisms give $\mathscr L_uQ_{V,\bullet}\simeq Q_{U,\bullet}$, respecting the full quotient diagram and the square. Step 3 identifies exchange at $\Delta K$ with $\Delta e$. Thus the first composite in the coherence theorem is $WH^a$, while the second is $H'^a\mathcal R_{Y'}^a(e)$. Its stated equality gives
$$WH^a=H'^a\mathcal R_{Y'}^a(e),\qquad W=v^a.$$
Here right composition with the specified inverse of $H^a$ gives the second equation. The inverses in the item exist: their evaluations are perfect projection-formula isomorphisms; their cones have zero evaluated cohomology and hence zero cohomology diagram. This uses conservativity for isomorphisms from levelwise exactness, never faithfulness of evaluations on morphisms.

source.place: Second paragraph: exchange/projection-formula equality; Stacks 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, supplied by the cited coherence node

proof.text:
Before composing with $\rho_K$, let $b,d$ be the two composites of $p_u,d_u$ for the corners at $r_X\mathcal R_X^aK$. Transpose $d\,r(W)b^{-1}$ under $G_{f'}\dashv R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}$. The adjunct clause of flat diagram restriction replaces its counit by the constant-coefficient counit. Pullback composition is also identified: its K-flat representative multiplies nested extension scalars, and after restriction both routes are the same composite inverse-image identification; the coefficient composition compatibility identifies their ring actions. Consequently its transpose is
$$G_{g'}\varepsilon_f^{\mathcal T}\circ\theta^{\mathcal T}_{\square,R_f^{\mathcal T}r_X\mathcal R_X^aK}.$$
This is precisely the transpose defining $E^{\mathcal T}_{r_X\mathcal R_X^aK}$. The adjunction bijection gives $d\,r(W)=E^{\mathcal T}b$. Compose with $R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}G_{g'}\rho_K$ and use naturality of this mate for $\rho_K$; with Step 6 and the definitions of $\beta,\delta$ this is
$$\delta\,r(v^a)=E^{\mathcal T}_{\mathcal R_X\bar K}\beta.$$
All equalities are in the derived strict-diagram category and hold for every complete $K$.

source.place: Second paragraph: strict mate comparison; expanded adjunct argument corresponding to normalization lemma Steps 6–7

proof.text: Only now assume the additional properness and the levelwise etale-origin witnesses in the strict-tower exchange normalization lemma. Its statement specifies $B_\bullet,D_\bullet$ as precisely $B^a,D^a$ and $v'_\bullet=H'^a\mathcal R^a(e)(H^a)^{-1}=v^a$. Its $b,d$ are normalized by the same restricted inverse images and the same K-injective direct images as Step 1. Therefore the $\beta,\delta$ of Step 4 are those $b,d$ followed by the images of $\rho_K$. The ordered completed base-change definition has source map $\mathcal L^a(H^a)r_S=s^a$, tower map $v^a$, and target comparison $c^a$ with the same direction. Substitution gives exactly $x^a_K=(c^a)^{-1}\mathcal L^a(v^a)s^a$. Since this expression was constructed before witnesses, it is independent of which witnesses are supplied. No assertion of that lemma was applied to an unwitnessed input.

source.place: Second paragraph: identification of the raw ordered expression with the witnessed construction

proof.text:
We fix the completed comparison by its unit. Let $L$ be complete on $V$, and put $j^a_{u,L}:Lu_a^*L\to F_u^aL$. By the completed-pullback definition and Koszul reconstruction, this is quotient completion, with its canonical unit. The constant-completion equivalence identifies this unit with the constant coefficient completion unit. With the strict pullback/reduction comparison of Step 4 and $\lambda$ of Step 2, set
$$\Psi_{u,L}=\mathcal L(\rho_{u,L})\lambda\,r_U(r_{u,L}):r_UF_u^aL\longrightarrow\mathcal L G_u\mathcal R_Vr_VL=F_u^0r_VL.$$
Here $r_{u,L}$ is the defining reconstruction into $\mathcal L^a\mathscr L_u\mathcal R_V^aL$. All factors are isomorphisms. The two maps out of the uncompleted pullback satisfy
$$\Psi_{u,L}\,r_U(j^a_{u,L})=j^0_{u,r_VL}\,a_{u,L}.$$
Indeed they arise from the identical strict map from the constant representative to its quotient diagram: Step 4 sends $p$ to its same class at every level WITH its transitions, and Step 2 takes the same limit after restriction. Thus this is equality of induced completion-unit maps, not an argument from evaluated equalities. The reflector node supplies bijectivity of precomposition with this unit for maps into any complete object; Koszul reconstruction identifies its unit with the quotient unit being used.

source.place: Second paragraph: reconstruction conjugations; Stacks 099M (lemma-naive-completion), 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), and 099B (lemma-derived-completion)

proof.text: The unit identity in Step 9 identifies $\Psi_{u,L}$ with the stipulated $\phi_{u,L}$, as follows. For complete $N$ on $U$, the two completed-adjunction Hom bijections first precompose with $j^a_{u,L}$ or $j^0_{u,r_VL}$ and then use the ambient adjunction. Step 1's adjunct clause says the second operations agree under $a_u,\chi_u$; Step 9's identity says the first operations agree under $\Psi_u$. Equivalences on complete objects are fully faithful by constant-completion equivalence. Hence $\Psi_u$ respects exactly these Hom bijections and is the isomorphism defining $\phi_u$ in (1). Uniqueness also follows directly from the reflector's injective precomposition map. Taking identities under these Hom bijections identifies the units and counits. Direct image preserves completeness by the direct-image-limits node (and on the constant side by completed-pullback-adjunction); thus the adjunctions are on the full complete subcategories as required. Finally the explicit conjugate formula, using just the identified units and counits, carries the specified direct-image composition and identity maps to their corresponding completed pullback comparisons. This proves all of (1).

source.place: Second paragraph: units, counits and fixed adjunction-conjugate normalization

proof.text:
Apply $\Psi=\phi$ from Steps 9–10 to $(u,L)=(g',K)$. Its defining formula is precisely
$$\mathcal L(\rho_{g',K})\lambda\,r(r_{g',K})=r_{g',K}^0\phi_{g'}.$$
For the source apply it to $(u,L)=(g,Rf_*K)$; this input is complete by direct-image-limits. Replace $r_YRf_*K$ by $R_f^0\bar K$ through $\chi_f$. Naturality of the completion unit and of its strict quotient diagram gives the comparison $F_g^0\chi_f$ on completed pullbacks and $\mathcal R(G_g\chi_f)$ on the reduction diagram. By Step 4 their composite on the latter diagram is exactly $\rho_M$. With the source reconstruction $r_S$ this yields
$$\mathcal L(\rho_M)\lambda_{\mathcal R^aM}\,r(r_S)=r_S^0(F_g^0\chi_f)\phi_g=r_S^0\iota_S.$$
For clarity the equality of these extensions can be tested by precomposing with the completion unit, where both maps are the strict quotient map followed by $G_g\chi_f$; injectivity of unit precomposition into a complete target, supplied by the reflector, proves the equality. This derives both fixed reconstruction equations in (3).

source.place: Second paragraph: the two specified reconstruction normalizations

proof.text:
The source normalization now follows by functoriality. Since $s^a=\mathcal L^a(H^a)r_S$, naturality of $\lambda$ and Step 5 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L(\beta)\lambda_{B^a}r(s^a)
&=\mathcal L(\beta\,r(H^a))\lambda_{\mathcal R^aM}r(r_S)\\
&=\mathcal L(H^0)\mathcal L(\rho_M)\lambda_{\mathcal R^aM}r(r_S)\\
&=\mathcal L(H^0)r_S^0\iota_S=s^0\iota_S.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality uses exactly the definition of $s$ in completion-mate-comparison, so an arbitrary source isomorphism has not been substituted.

source.place: Second paragraph: conjugation by the source projection-formula and reconstruction maps

proof.text:
For the target put $u=f'$ and $Z=\mathscr L_{g'}\mathcal R_X^aK$, and abbreviate $\rho_{g',K}$ to $q$. The definitions give
$$c^a=\kappa_u^a(Z)Ru_*(r_{g',K}),\quad
\delta=(R_u^{\mathcal T}q)d_{u,Z},\quad
t^0=\kappa_u^0(G_{g'}\mathcal R_X\bar K)R_u^0(r_{g',K}^0).$$
Use the comparison square of Step 2, followed by naturality of $\kappa_u^0$ for $q$ and of $\chi_u$ for $r_{g',K}$. It gives, in the written order,
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L(\delta)\lambda_{D^a}r(c^a)
&=\kappa_u^0(G_{g'}\mathcal R_X\bar K)\,
R_u^0\bigl(\mathcal L(q)\lambda_Zr(r_{g',K})\bigr)\chi_{u,F_{g'}^aK}\\
&=\kappa_u^0(G_{g'}\mathcal R_X\bar K)R_u^0(r_{g',K}^0\phi_{g'})\chi_{u,F_{g'}^aK}\\
&=t^0(R_u^0\phi_{g'})\chi_{u,F_{g'}^aK}=t^0\iota_T.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is the target reconstruction identity of Step 11. The direct-image-limits statement and completion-mate-comparison specify their $c^a,t^0$ by the K-injective direct-image/limit comparison used in Step 2. Thus this calculation proves compatibility of those specified comparisons, including $\chi,\lambda,\delta$, rather than assuming a finite-reduction normalization.

source.place: Second paragraph: fixed target direct-image/limit normalization

proof.text:
Apply $\mathcal L$ to Step 7 and use naturality of $\lambda$. Substitute the source and target normalizations of Steps 12–13 into $x_K^a=(c^a)^{-1}\mathcal L^a(v^a)s^a$ and cancel the isomorphisms in order:
$$\begin{aligned}
\iota_Tr(x_K^a)
&=(t^0)^{-1}\mathcal L(\delta)\lambda_{D^a}\,r(\mathcal L^a(v^a))r(s^a)\\
&=(t^0)^{-1}\mathcal L(\delta\,r(v^a))\lambda_{B^a}r(s^a)\\
&=(t^0)^{-1}\mathcal L(E^{\mathcal T})\mathcal L(\beta)\lambda_{B^a}r(s^a)\\
&=(t^0)^{-1}\mathcal L(E^{\mathcal T})s^0\iota_S.
\end{aligned}$$
All transformations in the construction are natural: the scalar and finite-reduction comparisons, the adjuncts, completion units, and the K-injective limit comparisons. The displayed derivations are operations on those transformations, hence hold naturally for every morphism of complete $K$. Completed pullback lands in the complete category by its reflector description, and direct image preserves that category; the same proof therefore applies to those intermediate complete inputs. Completion-mate-comparison identifies the right-hand expression with the completed constant-coefficient mate; its Noetherian and perfect-quotient hypotheses are those of the datum. No identity-square or pasting law is used.

source.place: Second paragraph: final ordered conjugation, naturality and complete intermediate inputs
